chunks: Suleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayoob al-Lakhmy narrated that Abdul Wahab ibn Kharajat said: Abu Kurayb narrated that Ali ibn Hafs al-Abasi narrated that Al-Hassan ibn al-Hussein al-Alavi, from his father Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, from Al-Hussein ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
I swear by Him in whose Hand is my soul that no two things have been combined better than forbearance (hilm) with knowledge ('ilm).

key_terms.الَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ: I swear by Him in whose Hand is my soul (a common prophetic oath formula).
key_terms.حِلْم: Forbearance, patience, or gentleness in dealing with others despite having the power to react harshly.
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّم: Peace be upon him and his family (SAWW).
key_terms.عِلْم: Knowledge, specifically religious or divine knowledge.

ai.seo_question: What is the best combination of virtues according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the synergy between theoretical knowledge (*'ilm*) and practical moral restraint (*hilm*), where wisdom without patience is incomplete. It reflects the Prophetic tradition that true leadership and piety require the integration of deep understanding with the temperance to apply it justly. This pairing is often cited in Shia ethical discourse as the foundation of the *Ahl al-Bayt*'s character.
